newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha static due to Singapore holiday.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha static due to Singapore holiday.

text.p: Naphtha prices were stable in lacklustre Tokyo trade on Wednesday with the Singapore market closed for a national holiday, market participants said.
"Trading is as good as dead," one naphtha trader said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half July was notionally assessed at $214.00/215.50 per tonne. It was sold to a European major at $214.50 in late Tuesday trading.
First-half August was quoted at $215.00/216.50 after it was traded once at $216.00, and again at $215.25 on Tuesday.
Inter-month naphtha spreads remained unchanged, with second-half July/second-half August traded at minus $1.75.
Near-term naphtha spreads are expected to remain in contango at least for the time being as arbitrage cargoes continued arriving from the West, traders said.
In the physical market, trading for first-half July delivery is expected to pick up toward the end of the week now that term talks with Saudi Aramco are almost over, they said.
A 275,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker at Indonesia's Dumai refinery was rumoured to have resumed its operations, setting a bullish tone in the low sulphur waxy residue market.
The unit has been closed since a fire at the plant in April. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
